options.impactSummary: No metadata changes; the story stays unmet.
options.summary: Leave the build as it is. The build does not meet the story: new cases are never assigned and the rotation position is not kept between transactions.
options.title: Do nothing

tradeOffs.note: Confirmed: CaseTrigger fires on before update and after update only (demo/org/force-app/main/default/triggers/CaseTrigger.trigger:1), so no code runs when a case is created; AC-1, AC-3, AC-4 and AC-6 are not met.

Confirmed: CaseAssignmentService.assign only picks cases moved back to New during an update (demo/org/force-app/main/default/classes/CaseAssignmentService.cls:21-22), and its position restarts every transaction (CaseAssignmentService.cls:7-8, :33), so AC-2 is not met.

options.impactSummary: Touches the Case trigger, its handler, the assignment service and both test classes, adds one rotation-state object and field, and grants access to it in two permission sets.
options.summary: Add before insert to CaseTrigger and a BEFORE_INSERT branch in CaseTriggerHandler that calls a new insert entry point on CaseAssignmentService. The entry point reuses agentPool() and reads and writes the last assigned agent on a new rotation-state record, so the next save continues the rotation. It assigns only cases whose OwnerId is still the creator, so an explicit owner is kept (AC-7, OQ-11).
options.title: Insert-time assignment in CaseAssignmentService with a stored rotation position

tradeOffs.note: Confirmed: reuses agentPool(), which already returns active direct users of the Escalation_Agents queue (CaseAssignmentService.cls:42-67, IsActive filter at :62) for AC-4, and the empty-pool return (CaseAssignmentService.cls:30-31) for AC-5. The service has no record-type filter (CaseAssignmentService.cls:18-67), so Premium_Support cases join the rotation (AC-6). The queue itself is in source (demo/org/force-app/main/default/queues/Escalation_Agents.queue-meta.xml:3) but has zero hits in the index, so it is not listed as a component.

Inferred: assign() calls oldMap.get (CaseAssignmentService.cls:21), which fails when oldMap is null on insert, so insert needs its own entry point and the update path stays as it is (OQ-3); the existing update tests (CaseAssignmentService_Test.cls:72, CaseTriggerHandler_Test.cls:57) must keep passing. The register shows in-flight entries on these components only for DEMO-202 itself (commit 121a920, the older impact record being replaced); no other squad is changing them.

Inferred: the project rule requires user-mode DML (CaseAssignmentService.cls:51, :62 already query WITH USER_MODE), so every user who creates a case needs read and edit on Round_Robin_State__c. Service_Agent and Team_Lead grant Case create (Service_Agent.permissionset-meta.xml:44-49, Team_Lead.permissionset-meta.xml:44-49) and need the new object access. Integration or other creators outside these permission sets are Unverifiable (org-only; Salesforce Admin, OQ-8).

Inferred: per transaction one pool lookup (two queries, CaseAssignmentService.cls:47-62), one read and one write of the state record, none inside a loop, so a 200-case load (AC-3) is spread in one pass. Two saves at the same moment can read the same position unless the state read locks the record (FOR UPDATE); the locking approach is for the Tech Lead to confirm.
Unverifiable: case volumes and peak bulk loads are org data and were deferred (OQ-8, Salesforce Admin); lock contention on the single state record at peak cannot be judged from the repo.
Confirmed: zero hits in index for Logger, so there is no project logger to reuse for assignment failures; whether to add one is for the Tech Lead.

options.impactSummary: Touches the Case trigger, its handler, the assignment service and both test classes, with no new metadata.
options.summary: Same trigger and handler change as OPT-2, but the new insert entry point finds the owner of the most recently created case owned by a pool member and starts the rotation after that agent, with no new metadata to hold the position.
options.title: Insert-time assignment that derives the next agent from the latest assigned case

tradeOffs.note: Confirmed: reuses agentPool() (CaseAssignmentService.cls:42-67) and the handler dispatch (CaseTriggerHandler.cls:13-24) with no new object, field or permission set change.

Inferred: the class is with sharing and queries WITH USER_MODE (CaseAssignmentService.cls:10, :51, :62), so a creator who cannot see the latest case under the org's sharing settings gets a wrong start position and AC-2 can fail. Sharing is org configuration and Unverifiable (Salesforce Admin, OQ-8).

Inferred: the latest case owner is also changed by the update-path re-assignment (CaseAssignmentService.cls:34-37) and by manual owner changes, so the derived position drifts from the rotation; behaviour is harder to reason about and to test than a stored position.
Inferred: one extra query on Case per transaction, outside any loop; concurrent saves can read the same latest case, the same race as OPT-2 but without a record to lock (Tech Lead).

reasons: Provisional, pending confirmation by a named owner: OPT-2 is the only option that keeps the rotation position between transactions independent of record visibility, which AC-2 needs; OPT-3 depends on the creator seeing the latest case under with sharing and USER_MODE (CaseAssignmentService.cls:10, :51, :62).

Reuses the existing pool, inactive-user filter and empty-pool behaviour (CaseAssignmentService.cls:30-31, :42-67) for AC-4 and AC-5, and the existing dispatcher (CaseTriggerHandler.cls:13-24), while leaving the update path unchanged per OQ-3.

A stored state record gives a single row that can be locked for concurrent saves (governor-limits trade-off); the lock approach and the new permission-set access (security trade-off) remain for the Tech Lead and Salesforce Admin to confirm.
